dhpak2.2:1.1: The story title was corrected to include seṭṭhi (‘Rich Man’) from the Pāli heading.
dhpak2.2:3.3: dāsakammakaro names slaves and workers, not slaves alone.
dhpak2.2:4.7: mātāpitaro vanditvā says the son paid homage to his parents, not merely that he bade them farewell.
dhpak2.2:6.2: bhattavetanaṃ is payment in food, not specifically rice.
dhpak2.2:7.1: sabbaravaññū says Bimbisāra understood all sounds, rather than recognized anyone by voice.
dhpak2.2:7.5: bhatakānaṃ bhatikārako identifies a hired worker among hired workers, not a servant of servants.
dhpak2.2:10.6: dve tīṇi sūpabyañjanāni says two or three portions of sauce and curry, not three.
dhpak2.2:11.1: muducittataṃ says Kumbhaghosaka's heart had softened, not that his senses were dull.
dhpak2.2:12.2: The Pāli says he sat on the bed (nisinnamatte), rather than lay down, when it sank.
dhpak2.2:12.6: The cuts were made over two or three days (dve tayo divase), not three successive days.
dhpak2.2:13.2: The Pāli says he sat on the bed (nisinnamatte) when it later collapsed, rather than lay down.
dhpak2.2:19.2: mahādhanaṃ vañcetvā khādasī concerns concealing his wealth while living as he did, not deceit in spending it.
dhpak2.2:19.6: aho bālomhi is ‘What a fool I am,’ not ‘Alas, I am lost.’
dhpak2.2:21.2: dhitimā praises Kumbhaghosaka's steadfastness, not his wisdom.
dhpak2.2:22.2: corikādikammaṃ ... idhaloke ceva ... paraloke ca says wrongdoing oppresses and harms in this world and the next.
dhpak2.2:22.3: kasiṃ vā bhatiṃ vā permits farming or hired work, not hired work alone.
dhpak2.2:22.5: kāyavācāhi concerns body and speech; the former English had added thoughts to that phrase.
dhpak2.2:22.6: issariyaṃ vaḍḍhati says prosperity grows, not that the man goes from strength to strength.
